33.interpretation: This verse illustrates the inevitable judgment of God on those who persist in sin. Jezebel, a symbol of rebellion against God, meets a tragic end, reminding us that evil cannot escape divine judgment.
33.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God is just and does not leave sin unpunished. The end of Jezebel reminds us of the importance of living a life that honors God, for the consequences of sin are real. We are called to flee from evil and seek holiness, knowing that God is sovereign and will judge the works of each.

mots.sens: This word means 'cursed' or 'detestable.' It comes from the root 'מאס' which evokes rejection or abomination. In this context, it highlights the contempt that Jehu feels for Jezebel, an emblematic figure of idolatry and opposition to God. Spiritually, it reminds us of the importance of turning away from anything that opposes divine will.

This term means 'daughter.' It is often used in the Bible to refer to lineage or family heritage. In this verse, it emphasizes Jezebel's position as a king's daughter, which accentuates her status and the gravity of her judgment. It teaches us that even those with high status are not above divine justice.

This word means 'to bury' or 'grave.' It is related to funeral practices and how bodies are treated after death. In the context of this verse, it indicates how Jehu orders the treatment of Jezebel's body, highlighting the irony of her royal status in light of her fate. It reminds us of the equality of all before death and the importance of living according to God's principles.

34.epoque: This passage is set in the 9th century B.C., a period marked by political instability and idolatry in Israel, with Jehu taking power after being anointed king.
34.passage: In this chapter, Jehu is purging the kingdom of Israel from the harmful influence of Jezebel and the house of Ahab, thus fulfilling God's prophetic judgment against these leaders.
34.culture: The culture of the time valued royal status and funeral rites, but Jehu shows that social position does not spare one from divine judgment. The burial of Jezebel, although planned, is filled with contempt.
34.interpretation: This verse illustrates the tragic end of Jezebel, a symbol of rebellion against God. Spiritually, it teaches us that rejection of God and His ways leads to destruction, regardless of the status or power one holds.
34.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of living in accordance with God's principles, regardless of our status or heritage. Jehu, by ordering the burial of Jezebel, teaches us that sin and rebellion against God have inevitable consequences. As believers, we must be careful not to be influenced by values contrary to divine will.

mots.sens: This word literally means 'skull' and is often associated with notions of death and judgment. In the biblical context, it evokes the ultimate defeat of the enemy, symbolizing the consequence of sin. Spiritually, it reminds us that physical death is not the end, but a passage to divine judgment.

This term means 'palm' or 'hand,' representing human action and work. In the Bible, the hand is often a symbol of power and authority. In this verse, it evokes the actions of Jezebel, emphasizing that her works have been judged and brought to nothing.

This word means 'foot' and is often related to the walk or path one chooses. In a spiritual sense, it can symbolize a person's life journey. The feet of Jezebel, found without the rest of her body, illustrate the tragic end of her life marked by idolatry and rebellion against God.

35.epoque: This passage is set in a period of political and spiritual transition in Israel, marked by the rise of Jehu and the fall of the house of Ahab. It is a time of divine judgment on those who led the people into idolatry.
35.passage: In 2 Kings 9, Jehu is anointed king of Israel and receives the mission to judge the house of Ahab. This verse describes the end of Jezebel, an emblematic figure of rebellion against God, whose body is despised and torn apart, underscoring divine judgment.
35.culture: In Israelite culture, burial was a sacred act, and the fact that only parts of Jezebel's body were found illustrates her dishonor and disgrace. It also reflects the belief that the body, even after death, must be treated with respect.
35.interpretation: This verse reminds us that sin has serious consequences and that God's judgment is inevitable. The decomposition of Jezebel's body symbolizes the destruction of all that she represented, highlighting the importance of living according to God's ways.
35.commentaire: The account of Jezebel's death teaches us that life choices have eternal repercussions. As believers, we must examine our own lives and ensure that we walk in the light and not in darkness. The tragic end of Jezebel reminds us that God is just and will judge every act, urging us to live in accordance with His will.

mots.sens: This name means 'My God is Yahweh.' Elijah, as a prophet, embodies faithfulness to God and opposition to idolatry. His role as a servant of the Lord underscores the importance of divine proclamation and justice. In this verse, Elijah is the bearer of the prophetic word announcing God's judgment on Jezebel.

The term 'dogs' evokes animals often associated with decay and impurity in Israelite culture. In this context, their role in consuming the flesh of Jezebel symbolizes contempt and divine judgment. This underscores the seriousness of her sin and the certainty of God's judgment on those who oppose Him.

This name means 'God has sown' and evokes both fertility and judgment. The field of Jezreel is a place of confrontation between good and evil, where divine justice is exercised. This geographical context becomes the stage for the fulfillment of God's promises and judgments.

36.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the kingdom of Israel in the 9th century B.C., a period marked by apostasy and idolatry under the reign of Ahab and Jezebel.
36.passage: In this chapter, Jehu is anointed king of Israel and receives the mission to purge the kingdom of idolaters, particularly Jezebel. The prophetic declaration of Elijah is thus recalled to emphasize the legitimacy of Jehu's actions.
36.culture: In Israelite culture, death and judgment were often symbolized by animals like dogs, which were considered unclean. The manner in which Jezebel is judged also reveals the place of divine justice in society.
36.interpretation: This verse illustrates God's faithfulness to His promises and the certainty of His judgment on evil. Jehu, as an instrument of God, reminds us that the consequences of sin are inevitable and that divine justice is always fulfilled.
36.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God is just and keeps His promises. We must be vigilant against the idolatry and sins that surround us, for God's judgment is certain. As believers, we are called to live in truth and proclaim God's word, while remembering that divine justice is at work in our lives and in the world.

mots.sens: This term means 'manure' or 'fertilizer.' It evokes the idea of something degraded, worthless, returning to the earth. In the context of this verse, it highlights the humiliating fate of Jezebel, whose life and actions were marked by rebellion against God. Spiritually, this reminds us that those who oppose God ultimately end up being brought to nothing.

This word means 'to destroy' or 'to annihilate.' It is often used in the context of divine judgment. In this verse, it emphasizes the total destruction of Jezebel, who will leave no trace of her existence. This highlights God's justice, which does not leave sin and idolatry unpunished.

This term means 'to cease' or 'to stop.' In the context of this verse, it indicates that the memory of Jezebel will be completely erased. This underscores the seriousness of her actions and how God puts an end to the influence of evil. Spiritually, this reminds us that God has the power to extinguish all memory of those who oppose Him.

37.epoque: This passage takes place during the reign of Israel, at the time when Jehu is anointed king to eradicate the house of Ahab and its idols, notably Jezebel.
37.passage: Chapter 9 of 2 Kings recounts the rise of Jehu and his divine mandate to judge the house of Ahab. Verse 37 concludes the judgment pronounced against Jezebel, illustrating the consequence of her actions.
37.culture: In Israelite culture, respect for ancestors and the memory of individuals were very important. Being reduced to a state of dishonor like Jezebel was an extreme shame.
37.interpretation: This verse symbolizes the end of Jezebel's evil influence, representing idolatry and rebellion against God. It emphasizes that God's judgment is inevitable for those who persist in evil.
37.commentaire: The fate of Jezebel reminds us that actions have consequences, especially when they are in opposition to God's will. As believers, we must be careful not to allow idolatry or sin to take root in our lives, for God is just and judges evil. This passage encourages us to seek a life that honors God, so that our legacy is one of faithfulness and not shame.
